title: Learning, saxophone arpeggios and Bobby Hackett sitting in with Cab
summary: He never worried about his ideas being taken, had to purge saxophone arpeggios from his trumpet, and was upset by Bobby Hackett's one night with Cab.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Did you ever worry about someone taking your ideas?

No, no I didn't because I didn't think I had any ideas, I was too busy trying to learn, I didn't worry about those things. I never felt myself that good. You know I wanted to -- I was, as I said, confused. Very confused. I didn't know what I wanted to do. And being a saxophone player too, had a lot to do with my trumpet playing.
Well, because I was playing a lot of jazz saxophone and when you -- also and playing trumpet switching to trumpet you find yourself playing the same thing that you've playing on the saxophone.

Arpeggios the same arpeggios. I had to get all of that out of my system. And I was too busy learn- ing, I didn't worry about anyone listening to me, at that time. I was too busy. Bobby Hackett came on the scene, that was another problem. He worked with Cab one night.

Yes, we were up at Sunland (somewhere in New England) during that time, and I think one of our trumpet players was sick or something, Bobby came in and played. I never heard of Bobby Hackett. And he upset everybody. So I started buying his records. And going on like that. I never worried about anything like that. I was too busy, and I'm still the same way today. I hear too many things I'd like to do.
